channel.title: WSJ | World
channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: ‘Preparing to Fire’: Hear the Radio Commands Enforcing the U.S. Blockade of Iran
item.description: Audio recordings capture months of warnings, confusion and attacks in the U.S. Navy’s blockade of Iranian oil exports.

item.title: U.S. Escalates Pressure on Russia Over Siberia Lab Death
item.description: The U.S. has warned Moscow that its failure to disclose details about the death violates international health obligations.

item.title: U.S. Presses Russia for Details on Plague Lab Death
item.description: Plus, a former German spy chief was arrested on suspicion of espionage and Google and Constellation Energy struck a 20-year nuclear-power deal.

item.title: French Government Is Willing to Bypass Parliament to Pass Billions in Cuts
item.description: In an interview, French Finance Minister Roland Lescure said he is open to negotiation but will do “whatever it takes” to get the budget through.

item.title: Oil Futures Little Changed as Market Weighs Export Recovery, Shipping Risks
item.description: Oil prices staged a late recovery Tuesday, snapping a two-session losing streak as traders assessed recovering Middle East crude exports against fresh shipping incidents around the Strait of Hormuz and renewed fighting near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait.

item.title: Families of Dead Prospectors Sue Authority That Certifies Gold as Ethically Produced
item.description: The claimants said that after the killings, the London Bullion Market Association should have withheld stamp of approval for a Tanzanian mine.

item.title: Ebola Patient Boarded Commercial Flight, Died Shortly After Arrival
item.description: The man’s death is Kenya’s first reported fatality from Ebola’s Bundibugyo strain, which has killed more than 4,000 people in eastern Congo.

item.title: Inside the Albanian Village Fighting a Jared Kushner-Backed Luxury Resort
item.description: Watch how Zvernec residents are pushing back against plans to build hotels, casinos and a water park where villagers once farmed.

item.title: The Silent Electronic Battleground Shaping the Future of Warfare
item.description: From spoofing hypersonic missiles to jamming drone signals, combat zones are in the grip of an electronic arms race.

item.title: What We Know About the Death of the Russian Plague-Lab Worker
item.description: Scientists say that if the woman did die of plague, it is unlikely to have spread widely around Russia or to other countries.

item.title: U.S. Looks to Iceland as It Expands Military Footprint in Arctic
item.description: Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s visit seeks to deepen cooperation with a country rattled by President Trump’s threats against neighboring Greenland.

item.title: India Voter-List Purge Draws Growing Backlash
item.description: About 130 million people have been deleted from final or preliminary voter rolls in a process that some government critics have described as opaque.

item.title: Former German Spy Chief Arrested on Suspicion of Espionage
item.description: The arrest is one of the biggest scandals to engulf the BND spy agency since its creation in the mid-1950s.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts for October 2026: Up to 4.50%
item.description: These are the accounts that offer the best interest rates—without burdensome fees, gimmicks or other hassles

item.title: China’s Burned-Out Young Are Finding Something Unexpected in Mao
item.description: Plus, EU plans action against Chinese imports, Nike’s turnaround effort in China and a U.S. effort to loosen Beijing’s grip on critical minerals

item.title: Yemen’s Houthi Rebels Strike Two Airports in Saudi Arabia
item.description: The attacks follow a new counteroffensive by Saudi-backed forces seeking to push the rebels back from the Red Sea coast.

item.title: Hackers Use Chinese AI Tool to Hit South Korean Banks, Exposing New Risk
item.description: The attacks were the latest to highlight the vulnerability of even hardened targets to hackers using freely available artificial-intelligence tools.

item.title: France Spent for Years. Now the Bill Is Coming Due.
item.description: Plus, see how a reply-all email after Oct. 7 tore a business apart, and what Oura’s stalled IPO reveals about one-hit wonders.

item.title: Exporters to Get Extra Year for EU’s Methane Emission Rules, Von Der Leyen Says
item.description: Policymakers are racing to shield industry from the high cost of fuel triggered by conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine.

item.title: German Factory Orders Tumbled in August
item.description: Manufacturing orders in the eurozone’s largest economy fell 10.6% on month, as the conflict in the Middle East kept energy costs elevated.
